title.narrative: Improving Services for Victims of Gender Based and Domestic Violence

description.narrative: The Development Objective for this project is to support the Solomon Islands to improve access to services in favor of women faced with Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and in particular Domestic Violence (DV). The Project has two components: 1) Workshop and Diagnostic Study on Services Available for Victims of Domestic Violence; and 2) Pilot Subproject to address core capacity by frontline responders in particular focused on standardized provision of services to victims of GBV and DV. Domestic violence in the Pacific undermines economic and social development, affecting women’s well-being and undermines their children’s welfare. A 2009 study revealed that 64 % of Solomon Islands women between 15 and 49 have experienced physical or sexual violence, or both, by an intimate partner. By international standards, the Solomon Islands perform poorly on gender equality, ranking 129 out of 177 countries on the Gender and Development Index. Until very recently, the Solomon Islands had no women in Parliament. With only one woman Member of Parliament (out of 50 members) and only 7% of senior positions in the public service, the Solomon Islands face very serious gender disparities. Both GBV and DV have widespread negative implications for a country’s economic and social development, as affecting the health, well-being, social engagement and labor integration of women, who are victims of GBV and DV. In addition, the health, nutrition, well-being and education of their children is also negatively impacted thus affecting the social and economic development of future generations. Government Commitment to Gender and Eliminating Gender Violence There is a strong commitment to improve gender equality and eradicate gender based violence in Solomon Islands. In 2007, the Government created the Ministry for Women, Youth, Children and Family Affairs (MWYCFA) to elevate gender issues in the country. Although small and new, MWYCFA has embarked on an ambitious policy agenda to empower women through the Gender Equality and Women’s Development Policy and a national sub-policy to eliminate violence against women. This sub-policy addresses seven key strategic areas. There include: developing national commitments to eliminate GBV; strengthening legal frameworks, law enforcement and justice systems; eliminating and preventing GBV through public awareness and advocacy; improving protective, social and support services; treating perpetrators; working with men to end GBV; and improving policy coordination across the spectrum.
